name: Knoxville
headline: Deck and porch staining in Knoxville, from Fourth and Gill to South Knox
lede: The city has some of the oldest porches in East Tennessee and some of the shadiest backyards. We work both.

sections.p: In Fourth and Gill, Old North and Parkridge, the porches are often a hundred years old and have been painted more times than anyone can count. A stain won't hold on that. We figure out what's on there first, then either prep it for paint or strip it back for stain. We'll tell you honestly which makes sense.

South Knoxville's ridges and hollows put a lot of decks under trees. Those boards stay wet, go green and get slick. We spend most of the job on cleaning and drying, and pick a stain that holds up to mildew.
Bigger homes along the river tend to have big decks and long railings. We price railings separately so you can see where the money goes.

woodNotes: Shady, mildew-prone decks in South Knox

faq.q: My porch floor is painted. Should I stain it?
faq.a: Usually not. Old tongue-and-groove porch floors were made for paint. We'll look and tell you which finish will last.

name: Farragut
headline: Deck staining in Farragut subdivisions and lake homes
lede: West Knox County is mostly neighborhoods built from the '80s on, plus homes on Fort Loudoun Lake. The decks are big and the HOAs are particular.
imageAlt: Close view of wood deck boards

sections.p: Most Farragut decks are on their second or third stain job. If the last one was solid color and it's peeling, it has to come off before we start again. If it was semi-transparent, a good wash and a fresh coat is often all it takes.
Many neighborhoods here have approved color lists. Send it to us and try the colors on your own deck in the visualizer before you turn in the request.
Waterfront decks get morning fog and full afternoon sun off the lake. We plan for that with a mildew-resistant, well-pigmented stain and an honest schedule for touch-ups.

faq.q: Can you give me something to show my HOA?
faq.a: Yes. We'll send the color name and a picture of it on your deck from our visualizer, and bring a sample board if they want one.

name: Powell
headline: Deck staining in Powell
lede: North Knox County mixes older homes on bigger lots with newer subdivisions. A lot of the decks here have never been finished at all.
imageAlt: Wide wood deck with a bench

sections.p: We see a lot of pressure-treated decks in Powell that went straight from the builder to the weather. Gray and rough isn't the end. Cleaning and brightening usually brings them right back, and then they take stain well.
Bigger lots mean longer fences and the occasional shed or barn. If we're already set up for the deck, adding the fence is the cheapest time to do it.
Send a wide shot of the deck and a couple of close-ups. Most Powell decks we can price without a visit.

faq.q: My deck is 8 years old and never stained. Too late?
faq.a: Almost never. Unless boards are soft, a proper cleaning and brightener gets it ready for stain.

name: Maryville
headline: Deck staining in Maryville with a view of the Smokies
lede: Blount County homes face the mountains, so the decks face west and south, straight into the afternoon sun.
imageAlt: Wood deck and railing overlooking a wooded mountain valley

sections.h: Sun is the main enemy here
sections.p: A deck that faces the mountains usually faces the sun all afternoon. UV breaks finish down faster than rain. We lean toward a semi-transparent with good pigment, and away from clear sealers, which tend to quit after a season in full sun.
Hillside homes mean tall decks with long stairs. We price stairs and railings on their own lines so there's no guessing.
Older homes near downtown and Maryville College often have porches with years of paint. We'll tell you whether yours wants stain or paint.

woodNotes: West- and south-facing decks in full sun
Tall decks and long stairs on slopes

faq.q: Why does my mountain-view deck fade so fast?
faq.a: Because it faces the sun all afternoon. More pigment in the stain helps. So does a maintenance coat every couple of years before it wears through.

name: Seymour
headline: Cabin and deck staining in Seymour and the foothills
lede: On the way to the mountains: log homes, cabins and a lot of rental properties with decks that get heavy use.

sections.p: Logs check, move and soak up stain. We clean them, deal with the old finish, and brush stain into the checks and end grain where water gets in.
If you rent your cabin, a tired deck shows up in guest photos. Tell us your open dates and we'll schedule the work between bookings, weather permitting.
Cabin decks often have hot tubs and grills sitting on them. We work around them, and we'll point out any boards that are getting soft under the tub.

faq.q: Can you work between cabin rentals?
faq.a: Yes. Give us the open dates. Most cabin decks are two days; log walls take longer and we'll plan for that.

name: Oak Ridge
headline: Deck staining in Oak Ridge
lede: Oak Ridge was built fast in the 1940s. A lot of those small original homes have decks that were added decades later, and they need careful work.
imageAlt: Deck with wooden railing and chairs

sections.p: Many of the original houses got their decks later, built by different people over the years. We check the boards and rails before we stain and point out anything loose. A new finish shouldn't hide a problem.
The ridges are heavily wooded, so plenty of decks sit in shade and collect leaves. Expect a longer cleaning day and a mildew-resistant stain.
Homes near the lake deal with more moisture. We'll suggest a maintenance plan so you're recoating on time instead of stripping later.

faq.q: Is it worth staining an old add-on deck?
faq.a: If the frame is solid, yes. Cleaning, staining and a few new boards cost a fraction of a rebuild. If it isn't safe, we'll say so.
